mainTopic: Bathroom laws on שבת: כבוד הבריות and מוקצה, רב הונא's plowed field, ריש לקיש's grassy stone and the פרפיסא, and רבי יוחנן's ban on wiping with a חרס, including the כשפים story.
overview: This amud continues the laws of using the bathroom on שבת. First, רב חסדא allows carrying the wiping stones up to a rooftop bathroom because of כבוד הבריות. רבינא challenges this from the toothpick dispute, and the גמרא answers that a meal can be planned for but a bathroom need cannot. Next, the גמרא explains why רב הונא forbids relieving oneself in a plowed field on שבת: a person might fill in a hole, which is חורש. The גמרא then returns to ריש לקיש's ruling on a grassy stone. רב פפי tries to learn from it about the פרפיסא, רב כהנא rejects that, and אביי teaches when moving a פרפיסא is תולש or נוטע. Finally, the גמרא looks for the reason behind רבי יוחנן's ban on wiping with a חרס on שבת. It settles on רב נתן בר אושעיא's explanation and rejects רבא's hair-removal version. The amud ends with a story about a sorceress on a boat that explains the כשפים concern, and the story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: May one carry the wiping stones up to the roof?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא is asked whether a person may carry the wiping stones up to a rooftop bathroom on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Someone asked רב] חסדא: What is the law about carrying them (the stones for wiping) up with him to the roof?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone asks רב חסדא whether the stones that may be used for wiping on שבת may also be carried up to a bathroom on the roof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא allowed bringing stones into the bathroom for wiping. The new question is whether this permission also covers the extra effort of carrying them up to a roof. Stones are normally מוקצה, so this is a real question.

phrases.english: [Rav] Ḥisda:
phrases.notes: The end of the name of the one being asked; the beginning of the question is earlier.

phrases.english: What is [the law] about taking them up with him to the roof?
phrases.notes: 'Them' refers to the wiping stones discussed earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of wiping stones on שבת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the permission to handle wiping stones extend to carrying them up to a rooftop bathroom?

steps.title: Human dignity overrides the prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא permits it, because כבוד הבריות overrides a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Great is human dignity, since it pushes aside a prohibition of the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that carrying the stones up is allowed, because protecting a person's dignity is important enough to override a prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wiping properly is a matter of כבוד הבריות. That value is strong enough to override the prohibition of handling מוקצה stones. So the extra carrying is permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean כבוד הבריות overrides any Torah prohibition. The prohibition here (מוקצה) is rabbinic. It is called 'Torah' only because rabbinic law draws its authority from the verse of לא תסור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous principle that shows up in many areas of הלכה.

phrases.english: He said to him: Great is human dignity
for it overrides a prohibition in the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is permitted, because כבוד הבריות overrides the prohibition.

steps.title: מרימר teaches this ruling
steps.stepSummary: מרימר taught רב חסדא's ruling in the study hall.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר sat and stated this teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short story line that sets up the next move. מרימר repeats the ruling, and a challenge is about to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling of כבוד הבריות is now being taught publicly. This sets the stage for רבינא's objection.

phrases.english: Mareimar sat
and was stating this teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב מָרִימָר וְקָאָמַר לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a challenge to step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מרימר transmits the ruling that כבוד הבריות overrides the prohibition.

steps.title: רבינא challenges from the toothpick dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבינא cites a ברייתא where חכמים forbid taking a toothpick from the ground on שבת, even though it is for a person's comfort.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenged מרימר: רבי אליעזר says a person may take a wood chip from in front of him to clean his teeth. But חכמים say he may take one only from the animal's feeding trough!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the ruling. חכמים do not let a person take a toothpick lying on the ground, even though cleaning one's teeth is also about personal dignity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If כבוד הבריות overrides מוקצה, then חכמים should allow the toothpick. Instead, they allow only wood from the trough, which is already set aside for use. This suggests dignity does not override מוקצה.

phrases.english: Ravina raised an objection to Mareimar:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
A person may take a wood chip from what is before him
to clean his teeth with it,
and the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִטּוֹל אֶלָּא מִן הָאֵבוּס שֶׁל בְּהֵמָה!
phrases.english: He may take only from the animal's trough!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that כבוד הבריות overrides מוקצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חכמים forbid a מוקצה toothpick even though it serves personal dignity, so dignity does not seem to override מוקצה.

steps.title: A meal is planned, a bathroom is not
steps.stepSummary: The cases are different: a person can prepare a toothpick ahead of a planned meal, but cannot plan where he will need a bathroom.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare? There, a person sets a fixed place for his meal. Here, does a person set a fixed place for the bathroom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבינא's comparison. The toothpick case is different from the bathroom case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person knows ahead of time where he will eat, so he should have prepared toothpicks before שבת. A person cannot know in advance where he will need to relieve himself. That is why the bathroom case is a true need of כבוד הבריות.
steps.whatToRemember: כבוד הבריות overrides the rabbinic prohibition of מוקצה when the need could not have been prepared for. A toothpick could have been prepared in advance.

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, a person fixes a place for his meal,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא — אָדָם קוֹבֵעַ מָקוֹם לְבֵית הַכִּסֵּא?
phrases.english: here, does a person fix a place for the bathroom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The toothpick and the bathroom stones are the same kind of dignity need.
steps.terutzMaskana: A meal can be planned for, so toothpicks should be prepared ahead. A bathroom need cannot be planned for.

steps.title: רב הונא: no relieving oneself in a plowed field on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא forbids relieving oneself in a plowed field on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: It is forbidden to relieve oneself in a plowed field on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling: רב הונא says a person may not relieve himself in a plowed field on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling applies specifically to שבת. That means the reason must be a שבת-related concern, which the גמרא will now search for.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
It is forbidden to relieve oneself in a plowed field on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: אָסוּר לִפָּנוֹת בִּשְׂדֵה נִיר בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic related to bathroom laws on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relieving oneself in a plowed field on שבת is forbidden.

steps.title: What is the reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב הונא's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this is forbidden. This sets up a search through several possible reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason must explain why the ban applies only on שבת.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is relieving oneself in a plowed field forbidden specifically on שבת?

steps.title: Not because of trampling
steps.stepSummary: Trampling the furrows cannot be the reason, because then it would be forbidden on weekdays too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because of trampling (the furrows), it should be forbidden even on a weekday!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the reason is damaging the field by stepping on it, and rejects that idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Damaging someone's field is a concern every day of the week. Since רב הונא limited his ruling to שבת, this cannot be his reason.

phrases.english: If you say it is because of trampling,
then even on a weekday as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First suggested reason, rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would apply on weekdays too, but the ruling is limited to שבת.

steps.title: Not because of pulling up grass
steps.stepSummary: Detaching grass cannot be the reason, because ריש לקיש permits wiping with a stone that has grass growing on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because of grasses (that he might detach). But didn't ריש לקיש say: A stone with grasses growing on it may be used for wiping, even though one who pulls grass from it on שבת is liable to bring a חטאת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the worry is that he will tear off grass while wiping. It rejects this using ריש לקיש's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש allows wiping with a grassy stone on שבת, even though deliberately pulling the grass would be a Torah violation. Since wiping is permitted anyway, the grass concern cannot explain רב הונא.

phrases.english: Rather, because of grasses,
but didn't Reish Lakish say:
A stone on which grasses grew,
it is permitted to wipe with it.
And one who detaches from it on Shabbat is liable to a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם עֲשָׂבִים, וְהָאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second suggested reason, rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: ריש לקיש permits wiping with a grassy stone.

steps.title: The worry is filling a hole
steps.stepSummary: The real concern is that he will take dirt from a raised spot and throw it into a hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, perhaps he will take dirt from a high spot and throw it into a low spot, and he will be liable because of רבה's rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real reason. He might move dirt from a mound into a hole, which is a forbidden מלאכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a plowed field, there are mounds and dips. Leveling them by filling a low spot counts as a מלאכה on שבת, as רבה will explain next.

phrases.english: Rather, perhaps he will take from a high spot
and throw it into a low spot,
and he would be liable because of Rabba's [rule].

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דִילְמָא נָקֵיט מֵעִילַּאי וְשָׁדֵי לְתַתַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted reason after two rejections.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The concern is that he will fill in a hole in the field, which is a מלאכה.

steps.title: רבה: filling a hole is building or plowing
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that filling a hole is בונה in a house and חורש in a field.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה said: If someone had a hole and filled it in, in a house he is liable for building, and in a field he is liable for plowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבה's rule to support the reason just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leveling the ground improves it. In a house, that is like building a floor. In a field, it prepares the soil, like plowing. So filling a hole in a field on שבת is חורש.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא forbids relieving oneself in a plowed field on שבת out of concern that a person will fill in a hole, which counts as חורש.

phrases.english: As Rabba said:
If he had a hole and filled it,
in the house, he is liable for building;
in the field, he is liable for plowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That filling a hole in a field is a מלאכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה's ruling about filling a hole.

steps.title: Returning to ריש לקיש's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back ריש לקיש's ruling about the grassy stone in order to analyze it further.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning to the statement itself: ריש לקיש said: A stone with grasses growing on it may be used for wiping, and one who pulls grass from it on שבת is liable to bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to ריש לקיש's ruling, which was quoted only in passing above. It is setting up a discussion of that ruling itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word גופא signals that a ruling quoted earlier will now be studied on its own terms. The second clause, liability for a חטאת, shows that grass growing on a loose stone counts as attached and growing. Even so, ריש לקיש allows wiping with the stone.

keyTerms.meaning: to the matter itself (returning to a quoted statement)

phrases.english: To the matter itself: Reish Lakish said:
A stone on which grasses grew,
it is permitted to wipe with it.
And one who detaches from it on Shabbat is liable to a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the ruling quoted in step 9 for its own discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may wipe with a grassy stone, but pulling the grass from it is liable for a חטאת.

steps.title: רב פפי: a פרפיסא (perforated flowerpot) may be moved
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי infers from ריש לקיש that a פרפיסא may be carried on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said: Learn from ריש לקיש that this perforated flowerpot may be moved.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי draws a new law from ריש לקיש's ruling: a planted pot with holes in it may be moved on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a grassy stone may be picked up even though plants are growing on it, then a pot with plants growing in it should also be allowed to be moved. רב פפי treats the two cases as alike.

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said:
Learn from that of Reish Lakish:
this perforated pot is permitted to be moved.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פַּפֵּי: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִדְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Derives a new law from step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פרפיסא may be moved on שבת.

steps.title: רב כהנא: a need is not the same as no need
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא rejects the inference: the stone was permitted for a real need, but moving a flowerpot has no such need.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא objected: If they permitted it for a need, will they also permit it without a need?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא attacks רב פפי's comparison. The stone was allowed only because of the bathroom need.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving the grassy stone was permitted for wiping, which is a matter of כבוד הבריות. Moving a flowerpot for no such reason is a completely different situation, so nothing can be learned from the stone.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana strongly objected to this:
If they said [permitted] for a need,
will they say [permitted] not for a need?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפי's inference about the פרפיסא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The stone was allowed only for the need of wiping. A flowerpot is moved without such a need.

steps.title: אביי: moving a flowerpot can be detaching or planting
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that lifting a פרפיסא off the ground is תולש, and setting it down on the ground is נוטע.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Since the topic of the flowerpot has come up, let us say something about it. If it was on the ground and he put it on pegs, he is liable for detaching. If it was on pegs and he put it on the ground, he is liable for planting.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes the chance to teach two new laws about the פרפיסא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Through the holes, the plant draws nourishment from the ground. Lifting the pot off the ground cuts that connection, which counts as detaching. Setting it on the ground creates the connection, which counts as planting.

keyTerms.meaning: since it came to our hands

steps.whatToRemember: A פרפיסא draws from the ground through its holes. Lifting it off the ground is תולש, and placing it on the ground is נוטע.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
A perforated pot, since it has come to our hands,
let us say something about it:
If it was resting on the ground
and he placed it on top of pegs,
he is liable for detaching.
If it was resting on pegs
and he placed it on the ground,
he is liable for planting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: פַּרְפִּיסָא, הוֹאִיל וַאֲתָא לְיָדָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side-teaching prompted by the mention of the פרפיסא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lifting a פרפיסא from the ground is תולש. Placing it on the ground is נוטע.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: no wiping with a shard on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן forbids wiping with a חרס on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It is forbidden to wipe with an earthenware shard on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling: רבי יוחנן says not to use a piece of broken pottery for wiping on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once again the ruling is limited to שבת. The גמרא will now look for the reason.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
It is forbidden to wipe with an earthenware shard on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אָסוּר לְקַנֵּחַ בְּחֶרֶס בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about wiping on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wiping with a חרס on שבת is forbidden.

steps.title: Why is the shard forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this is forbidden. This sets up a list of possible reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As before, the reason must explain why the ban applies specifically to שבת.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is wiping with a חרס forbidden on שבת?

steps.title: Not because of danger
steps.stepSummary: Danger cannot be the reason, because the danger exists on weekdays too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because of danger, it should be forbidden even on a weekday!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the sharp edge is dangerous, and rejects that as the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sharp shard can cut a person on any day. That would not explain a ban limited to שבת.

phrases.english: If you say because of danger,
then even on a weekday as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First suggested reason, rejected.

steps.title: Not because of witchcraft
steps.stepSummary: Fear of כשפים cannot be the reason, because that also applies on weekdays.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, because of witchcraft. Then it should not be done even on a weekday!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that using a shard invites witchcraft, and rejects that as the reason as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A worry about witchcraft has nothing to do with שבת. It would forbid using a shard every day.

phrases.english: Rather, because of witchcraft,
then even on a weekday he should not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second suggested reason, rejected.

steps.title: Not because of removing hair
steps.stepSummary: Removing hair cannot be the reason, because it is a דבר שאין מתכוין, which is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, because of removing hairs. But that is an unintended act!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the shard might pull out hairs, which would be a שבת violation. It rejects this too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person does not intend to remove hair. An unintended result like this is a דבר שאין מתכוין, which is permitted, so it cannot be the reason for the ban.

phrases.english: Rather, because of removing hairs,
it is an unintended act.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third suggested reason, rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is a דבר שאין מתכוין, which is permitted.

steps.title: רב נתן בר אושעיא explains the ruling
steps.stepSummary: On a weekday the shard is plainly forbidden for the reasons already mentioned (danger and כשפים). רבי יוחנן mentions שבת to teach that it is forbidden even then, even though a shard is a כלי and the stones are מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נתן בר אושעיא said to them: A great man said something, so let us give a reason for it. It goes without saying that on a weekday it is forbidden. But on שבת, since the shard has the status of a utensil, I might think it is fine to use it. He teaches us that it is still forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נתן בר אושעיא explains why רבי יוחנן mentioned שבת. Even on שבת, the shard is still forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a weekday, a person can simply use a stone, so the shard, with its danger and כשפים concerns, is clearly forbidden. On שבת, one might think the shard is better because it counts as a כלי, while stones are מוקצה. רבי יוחנן teaches that those concerns still forbid it.
steps.whatToRemember: Wiping with a חרס is forbidden every day because of danger and כשפים. רבי יוחנן said 'on שבת' to teach that its status as a כלי does not make it permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: The words 'on שבת' do not mean it is permitted on weekdays. It is forbidden all the more so on weekdays, and שבת is the new point being taught.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב נָתָן בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Rav Natan bar Oshaya said to them:
A great man said something,
let us give a reason for it:
It is not necessary [to say] on a weekday that it is forbidden,
but on Shabbat,
since it has the status of a utensil,
[I might say] it is fine.
He teaches us [that it is forbidden].

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבְרָא רַבָּה אֲמַר מִילְּתָא, נֵימָא בָּהּ טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the search by bringing back the danger and כשפים reasons and explaining why שבת is mentioned.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is forbidden every day because of danger and כשפים. Mentioning שבת teaches that the shard's כלי status does not permit it.

steps.title: רבא teaches the reason as removing hairs
steps.stepSummary: רבא holds that רבי יוחנן's ban on wiping with a shard on שבת is because of pulling out hairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught רבי יוחנן's ruling as being because of the removal of hairs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of רבי יוחנן's reason. רבא says the problem is that wiping with a shard pulls out hairs. This sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20, the hair reason was rejected because removing hair here is a דבר שאין מתכוין, which is permitted. רבא says this really was רבי יוחנן's reason. If so, רבי יוחנן must hold that a דבר שאין מתכוין is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rava taught it
because of the removal of hairs,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings back the hair reason that was rejected in step 20, as רבא's version of the ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבא, רבי יוחנן forbids wiping with a shard on שבת because it pulls out hairs.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוחנן forbids the shard because of hair, he forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין. But he also rules like an unattributed משנה that lets a נזיר wash his hair even though hairs may fall out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא found a difficulty between one statement of רבי יוחנן and another. Did רבי יוחנן say it is forbidden to wipe with a shard on שבת? Then he holds that an unintended act is forbidden. But רבי יוחנן also said the הלכה follows an unattributed משנה, and we learned in a משנה: a נזיר may wash his hair and separate it with his fingers, but he may not comb it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא points out a contradiction inside רבי יוחנן's own words. One ruling suggests an unintended act is forbidden, and another suggests it is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר may not remove hair. Yet the unattributed משנה lets him wash and separate his hair, even though some hair may fall out by accident. It only forbids combing, which surely pulls hair. Since רבי יוחנן rules like an unattributed משנה, he should permit a דבר שאין מתכוין. That contradicts רבא's version of the shard ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: the הלכה follows an unattributed משנה
a person who took a vow not to cut his hair, among other things
washes and separates the hair with his fingers

steps.confusionAlert: The נזיר case is not about שבת at all. It is brought only to show what רבי יוחנן holds about a דבר שאין מתכוין.

phrases.english: and he found it difficult,
one statement of Rabbi Yochanan against another statement of Rabbi Yochanan:
Did Rabbi Yochanan say
it is forbidden to wipe with a shard on Shabbat?
This shows that an unintended act is forbidden.
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
The halacha follows an unattributed mishna?
And we learned in a mishna:
A nazir may wash his hair and separate it with his fingers,
but he may not comb it!
phrases.notes: Combing will surely pull out hair. Washing only might, so it is a דבר שאין מתכוין and is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's version from step 22 by showing it creates a contradiction in רבי יוחנן's views.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that רבי יוחנן's reason is the removal of hairs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The hair reason only works if a דבר שאין מתכוין is forbidden. But רבי יוחנן rules like the unattributed משנה of the נזיר, which permits a דבר שאין מתכוין.

steps.title: רב נתן בר אושעיא's explanation is the correct one
steps.stepSummary: Because of the contradiction, the hair version is rejected. The correct explanation is רב נתן בר אושעיא's.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear that the correct explanation is that of רב נתן בר אושעיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רבא's version and settles on the earlier answer of רב נתן בר אושעיא, as explained in step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hair reason forces רבי יוחנן to contradict himself, so it cannot stand. רב נתן בר אושעיא's approach avoids this problem: the shard is forbidden on weekdays because of danger and כשפים, and שבת is mentioned to teach that it is forbidden even then. That is true even though a shard is a כלי and the stones are מוקצה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's ban on wiping with a shard is because of danger and כשפים, not hair removal. The hair reason fails because רבי יוחנן holds that a דבר שאין מתכוין is permitted.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear
that it follows Rav Natan bar Oshaya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מְחַוַּורְתָּא כִּדְרַב נָתָן בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction from step 23 by rejecting רבא's version and returning to the answer from step 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The reason is danger and כשפים, which apply every day. רבי יוחנן mentions שבת to teach that it is forbidden even on שבת, despite the shard being a כלי.

steps.title: What is the witchcraft concern?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what כשפים has to do with wiping with a shard.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the witchcraft?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the witchcraft idea from step 19 and asks what it means. This sets up a story that will explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 mentioned כשפים as a possible reason, but did not explain the link between witchcraft and wiping with a shard. Now the גמרא wants that information.

phrases.english: What is the witchcraft?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the witchcraft concern mentioned in step 19 to explain it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How wiping with a shard is connected to witchcraft.

steps.title: Two sages on a boat refuse a matron
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a story: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא were on a boat, and a matron asked to sit with them. They refused.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like the story of רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא, who were traveling on a boat. A certain matron said to them: 'Let me sit with you!' They did not let her sit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story to explain the witchcraft concern. This part only sets the scene.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sages refuse to let the woman sit with them, probably for reasons of modesty. Her anger at being refused leads to what happens next.

keyTerms.meaning: a matron, a noblewoman (here, a sorceress)

phrases.english: Like this incident of Rav Chisda
and Rabba bar Rav Huna,
who were traveling on a boat.
A certain matron said to them:
Let me sit with you!
And they did not let her sit.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 25 through a story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer comes through a story. Its key point about the shard comes at the end of the story.

steps.title: A battle of spells on the boat
steps.stepSummary: The matron casts a spell and stops the boat. The sages say something and free it. She asks what she can do to harm them.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said a word and stopped the boat. They said a word and released it. She said to them: 'What can I do to you?'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The woman uses witchcraft against the sages, but they undo it. She then admits she cannot harm them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She stops the boat with a spell. The sages free it, according to the commentaries by saying a holy Name. Her question 'What can I do to you?' leads into her explanation of why her witchcraft has no power over them. That explanation continues on the next amud and is where the link to the shard is made.

keyTerms.meaning: a word (here, a spell or incantation)
she tied it up / stopped it

steps.confusionAlert: The story does not end here. Her question 'What can I do to you?' is answered in the next lines, and that answer explains the shard.

phrases.english: She said something
and stopped the boat.
They said something
and released it.
She said to them:
What can I do to you?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from step 26, building toward the explanation of the witchcraft concern.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not yet complete. Her question leads into the explanation, which continues on the next amud.
